svg.title: Map-cache CPU time
svg.desc: Accumulated browser and descendant CPU time, not utilization or real-time frame cost. Both engines use a zero-based 0 to 5,000 ms axis. Circles and squares are medians; whiskers span the min and max of three trials. This measures only map-cache reuse, separately from the other optimizations. Chrome 156.0.8078.48, button: original median 1,440, range 1,420–1,530 ms; candidate median 1,280, range 1,270–1,340 ms. Chrome 156.0.8078.48, segmented: original median 4,590, range 3,590–4,790 ms; candidate median 4,360, range 4,300–4,540 ms. Chrome 156.0.8078.48, mostly-unique: original median 2,730, range 2,710–2,820 ms; candidate median 2,770, range 2,770–2,850 ms. Firefox 157.0, button: original median 2,870, range 2,100–3,020 ms; candidate median 2,380, range 1,400–3,010 ms. Firefox 157.0, segmented: original median 4,770, range 2,880–4,840 ms; candidate median 4,560, range 4,300–4,630 ms. Firefox 157.0, mostly-unique: original median 1,850, range 1,830–1,870 ms; candidate median 1,870, range 1,810–1,900 ms. Button and segmented workloads used twelve cycles; the mostly-unique workload used 1,200 updates. New-map median: +1.5% Chrome · +1.1% Firefox. Ranges overlap; no statistical significance is claimed. Source: evidence.json; SHA-256: c0a594e4945862915435f7b7e2b859f2d87a61982de25674655336efbeb91c57
